label: HTML
blurb: Markup a browser reads as a page.
first: is the markup a browser reads as a page. The first orientation is this: the page is a document, and the tags around the words tell the browser what each part is. A tag is a name written between angle brackets.
outline: A tag names one part of the document, such as a heading or a paragraph. | A link is a tag that points at another page. | The words a person reads, and the tags around them, are both in the file. | A full document has a head and a body. These course lessons are the body piece.

label: JavaScript
blurb: Instructions a browser can run after a page is open.
first: is a language the browser can run. The first orientation is this: after a page is open, a short instruction can run, and the page can change. The outline of this course is drawn that way.
outline: A name can hold a value. | A function is a small set of steps with a name. | Those steps can change what the page shows. | The browser console is a place to try one line.

label: Python
blurb: A file of steps a helper runs from top to bottom.
first: is a language you run as a file of steps, from top to bottom. The first orientation is this: you start the file, and it can show a result or write another file. The small helpers in this course are that kind of file.
outline: A name can hold a value. | print shows a result. | An indented line belongs to the question above it. | A helper can read a table and write another file.
